# ♿ ACCESSIBILITY

<a name="top"></a>

**Usable by everyone, and fixable when it is not.**

_Report the barrier. We will remove it._

</div>

---

## 🎯 Our Commitment

Everyone should be able to use this project and take part in it, whatever the
way they see, hear, move, read or think. An accessibility barrier is a defect,
and we treat it like one.

- **Interfaces** this project provides aim to meet the
  [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
  at level **AA**: keyboard access, visible focus, sufficient contrast, text
  alternatives, and meaning never carried by colour alone.
- **Documentation** uses real headings in order, describes every image in its
  alt text, and gives every link text that makes sense out of context.
- **Command-line output** never relies on colour or emoji alone to say whether
  something passed or failed.

Where a part of the project falls short, it is listed as an open issue labelled
`type: accessibility`, so nobody has to rediscover it.

---

## 🧯 Reporting a Barrier

- **Open an issue** with the ♿ **Accessibility Report** form. It asks for what
  a maintainer needs to reproduce the barrier: the page or element, the
  assistive technology and browser you used, and what you expected.
- **Start a discussion** in the **Accessibility** category if you are not sure
  whether it is a defect, or want to suggest an improvement.

You do not need to know which WCAG criterion is involved, or how to fix it.
Describing what stopped you is enough.

> [!NOTE]
> **For maintainers:** GitHub does not create an **Accessibility** discussion
> category. Create one named **Accessibility**, so the form in
> `.github/DISCUSSION_TEMPLATE/accessibility.yaml` shapes it, or remove the
> discussion route above.

---

## ⏱️ What to Expect

Accessibility reports are triaged like bug reports: acknowledged, labelled, and
prioritised by how many people the barrier stops and how completely. A barrier
that blocks a task outright is fixed ahead of one that only slows it down. This
project is maintained on a best-effort basis, as [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md)
explains.
